papers.title: Detecting and Preventing Data Poisoning Attacks on AI Models
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the critical issue of data poisoning attacks on AI models, a growing concern in the ever-evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As advanced technology systems become increasingly prevalent across various sectors, the need for robust defence mechanisms against adversarial attacks becomes paramount. The study aims to develop and evaluate novel techniques for detecting and preventing data poisoning attacks, focusing on both theoretical frameworks and practical applications. Through a comprehensive literature review, experimental validation using the CIFAR-10 and Insurance Claims datasets, and the development of innovative algorithms, this paper seeks to enhance the resilience of AI models against malicious data manipulation. The study explores various methods, including anomaly detection, robust optimization strategies, and ensemble learning, to identify and mitigate the effects of poisoned data during model training. Experimental results indicate that data poisoning significantly degrades model performance, reducing classification accuracy by up to 27 % in image recognition tasks (CIFAR-10) and 22 % in fraud detection models (Insurance Claims dataset). The proposed defence mechanisms, including statistical anomaly detection and adversarial training, successfully mitigated poisoning effects, improving model robustness and restoring accuracy levels by an average of $15-20 \%$. The findings further demonstrate that ensemble learning techniques provide an additional layer of resilience, reducing false positives and false negatives caused by adversarial data injections. The findings of this paper contribute to the broader understanding of adversarial machine learning and provide actionable insights for practitioners in industries facing emerging threats to AI-based systems. By addressing the challenges of data poisoning attacks, this study aims to improve the security and reliability of AI models, ultimately fostering greater trust in AI technologies across critical applications.

papers.title: Robust and Adaptive Dual-Defense Framework Against Data Poisoning Attacks in Recommendation Systems
papers.abstract: Deep learning-based recommendation systems are highly vulnerable to data poisoning attacks, where adversaries manipulate user interactions to degrade model integrity. We hypothesize that combining an active robust loss with a passive GAN-based detection will significantly reduce poisoning impact in recommendation systems without sacrificing utility. We propose a robust and adaptive dual-defense framework: the active defense integrates a crafted loss function to mitigate poisoning effects while maintaining model performance. The passive defense employs a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based detection model to identify and filter poisoned data, enhancing detection accuracy and system security. The framework supports classical matrix factorization (MF) model and large language model (LLM)-based pipelines and scales to large datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple real-world datasets at varying poison rates show that our method outperforms representative defenses, consistently reducing attack success without sacrificing recommendation quality. The framework also admits a federated instantiation, where robust training and GAN-based detection run on clients and only privacy-preserving summaries are aggregated. The proposed method significantly improves the robustness and adaptability of recommendation systems under data poisoning attacks.

papers.title: Adaptive AI-Driven Learning Architecture for Real Time Detection and Prevention of Data Poisoning and Model Evasion Attacks
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has been integrated into cybersecurity systems particularly in cyber threat intelligence (CTI) and has significantly enhanced the detection, analysis, and mitigation of sophisticated cyber threats in real time in organisations. Unlike traditional static defence mechanisms, which rely on fixed rules or offline retraining, the proposed architecture empowers continuous dynamic learning capabilities to identify and mitigate attacks as they unfold ensuring the integrity and reliability of AI-driven CTI systems. AI models to self-heal and harden against evolving adversarial tactics. The primary goal is to enhance CTI operations by providing timely, accurate threat detection and robust mitigation thereby reducing the window of opportunity for attackers and improving overall cybersecurity posture. This article presents a comprehensive adaptive learning architecture with formalised threat models, architectural specifications, and empirical validation. Experimental evaluation using benchmark datasets (CIC-IDS2017 and VirusTotal) demonstrates that the system achieves 43.7% higher evasion detection accuracy than traditional static anomaly detectors, while maintaining processing latency below 5 milliseconds. The architecture successfully detects 89.1% of poisoning attacks and reduces false positive rates by 37.5% relative to baseline methods. The key contributions of this article include the design of an integrated adaptive learning system that simultaneously detects and prevents both data poisoning and model evasion attacks within cybersecurity AI models.

papers.title: Resilient Autonomy: Securing Intelligent Systems Against Adversarial Attacks
papers.abstract: As autonomous systems become central to mission-critical operations, their ability to withstand adversarial threats is crucial to ensuring trust, safety, and uninterrupted functionality. This paper introduces a comprehensive framework for resilient autonomy that proactively prevents, detects, and mitigates key adversarial challenges, including sensor spoofing, sensor manipulation, and machine learning model poisoning. We present a layered defense architecture that integrates adversarial robust learning, real-time anomaly detection, and secure control strategies to maintain reliable autonomous behavior in compromised environments. Our hybrid resilience model addresses both inference-time perturbations and upstream vulnerabilities in data acquisition and processing pipelines. The system employs adaptive decision logic and decentralized failover mechanisms to dynamically reconfigure operations upon detection of anomalies or suspicious behavior, thus preserving mission continuity. In addition, we embed explainable AI modules to enhance transparency, facilitate system diagnostics, and support operator trust. We validate the proposed framework using a suite of simulated adversarial scenarios across diverse autonomous agents, including drones, mobile robots, and vehicle models. Results demonstrate significant gains in threat resistance, operational stability, and recovery time when compared to conventional defenses. This work lays the foundation for building self-reliant, attack-aware autonomous systems that are capable of sustaining functionality under adversarial uncertainty.

summary: The retrieved literature highlights critical advancements in developing robust AI systems against data poisoning and adversarial attacks, focusing on defensive strategies, adversarial training, and resilience in autonomous systems. Key themes include innovative frameworks for detecting and mitigating data poisoning, the exploration of adversarial training as a defense mechanism, and the need for layered defense architectures in autonomous systems. However, limitations such as scalability, real-world applicability, and the need for comprehensive empirical validation remain, underscoring significant research gaps that warrant further exploration.
scholarly_positioning: Existing approaches to enhancing AI resilience against data poisoning and adversarial attacks primarily focus on specific methodologies, such as adversarial training and dual-defense frameworks, yet they often lack scalability and real-world applicability. Notably, while frameworks have shown promise in controlled environments, their effectiveness in dynamic, real-world scenarios remains underexplored, revealing a significant gap in empirical validation. This research aims to develop a comprehensive adaptive learning architecture that not only addresses these limitations but also integrates robust anomaly detection and real-time response mechanisms, thereby contributing to a deeper understanding of resilience in AI systems. By situating this work within the broader discourse on AI security, it seeks to reconcile the tension between theoretical robustness and practical deployment, ultimately advancing the field's capability to withstand evolving adversarial threats.
research_scope: This study will develop and evaluate an Adaptive Learning Architecture specifically designed to enhance the resilience of machine learning models against data poisoning attacks in recommendation systems. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the architecture will be tested against various data poisoning attack variants using datasets such as CIFAR-10 and real-world recommendation datasets. The control group will consist of standard machine learning models and existing adversarial training techniques. Primary outcomes will include detection accuracy and robustness against attacks, while secondary outcomes will assess response time and adaptation rates. This research aims to bridge the gap between theoretical robustness and practical deployment in real-world scenarios, providing empirical validation for the proposed adaptive mechanisms.
concept_definition:
{
  "Adaptive Learning Architecture": "A framework that enables machine learning models to adjust their learning strategies in response to new data and threats, enhancing resilience against attacks.",
  "Anomaly Detection": "A process that identifies unusual patterns in data that may indicate a data poisoning attack, measured by detection accuracy and false positive rate.",
  "Real-time Response Mechanisms": "Systems that allow models to react immediately to detected anomalies, assessed by response time and adaptation rate.",
  "Robust Learning": "A learning approach focused on maintaining model performance despite adversarial conditions or data corruption.",
  "Dynamic Learning": "An approach that allows models to continuously learn and adapt from new data inputs in real-time.",
  "Detection Accuracy": "The percentage of correctly identified anomalies relative to the total number of actual anomalies.",
  "False Positive Rate": "The proportion of normal instances incorrectly classified as anomalies.",
  "Response Time": "The duration taken by the system to react to detected anomalies.",
  "Adaptation Rate": "The speed at which the model adjusts its parameters or strategies in response to new data.",
  "Model Performance Metrics": "Quantitative measures that evaluate how well a model performs, including accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score.",
  "Robustness Against Attacks": "The ability of a model to maintain its performance levels when subjected to adversarial manipulations or data poisoning.",
  "Data Poisoning Attack Variants": "Different methods of corrupting training data to mislead the learning process of machine learning models.",
  "Non-Poisoned Data": "Clean, unaltered data used as a control to evaluate the impact of data poisoning.",
  "CIFAR-10": "A widely used dataset for training machine learning models, consisting of 60,000 32x32 color images in 10 classes.",
  "CIC-IDS2017": "A dataset containing network intrusion detection data, useful for evaluating security models.",
  "Real-world Recommendation Datasets": "Datasets derived from actual user interactions and preferences used to train recommendation systems.",
  "Scalability Issues": "Challenges related to maintaining model performance as the size of the data or the number of users increases.",
  "Real-world Applicability Challenges": "Difficulties in implementing theoretical models in practical scenarios due to environmental variability or data dynamics."
}

gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of various defensive strategies against data poisoning in specific contexts such as recommendation systems; however, they treat the scalability and real-world applicability of these defenses as secondary, leaving unclear whether the proposed methods can maintain performance in dynamic environments. This matters practically because the increasing sophistication of data poisoning attacks necessitates robust solutions that can adapt to evolving threats; therefore, this study investigates the development of an Adaptive Learning Architecture that integrates real-time anomaly detection and response mechanisms to enhance resilience against data poisoning in diverse AI applications.

theoretical_mechanism: The proposed research investigates the impact of an Adaptive Learning Architecture (independent variable) on the detection accuracy and robustness against data poisoning attacks (dependent variable) in recommendation systems. The architecture integrates real-time anomaly detection and response mechanisms, which serve as mediators in enhancing system-level outcomes such as robustness against attacks and detection accuracy. The theoretical framework is grounded in resilience theory, positing that adaptive systems can better withstand adversarial threats through continuous learning and anomaly management. Assumptions include that the architecture's effectiveness is contingent on the quality of the anomaly detection algorithms and the adaptability of the learning mechanisms. Empirical validation is required to confirm the causal chain from adaptive learning strategies to improved system performance, while user-level outcomes such as trust and satisfaction may also be influenced by perceived transparency in the system's responses.
hypothesis: The implementation of an Adaptive Learning Architecture with real-time anomaly detection mechanisms will significantly improve detection accuracy compared to standard machine learning models, leading to enhanced robustness against data poisoning attacks in recommendation systems.

proposal: This research proposal aims to develop an Adaptive Learning Architecture within the domain of machine learning method development, specifically targeting the enhancement of AI resilience against data poisoning attacks in recommendation systems. Key concepts include 'Anomaly Detection', defined as the identification of unusual patterns indicating potential attacks, and 'Real-time Response Mechanisms', which allow immediate system reactions to anomalies. The study is technically feasible, assuming access to labeled datasets like CIFAR-10 and real-world recommendation datasets, as well as necessary computational resources. Current literature reveals a significant gap in addressing the scalability and real-world applicability of existing defenses against data poisoning, as many frameworks focus on controlled environments without empirical validation in dynamic settings. This study investigates how the proposed architecture improves detection accuracy and robustness compared to standard machine learning models and existing adversarial training techniques. The theoretical mechanism posits that the architecture enhances system-level outcomes (detection accuracy and robustness) through mediators (real-time anomaly detection and response mechanisms), while user-level outcomes may include trust and satisfaction influenced by perceived transparency. The falsifiable hypothesis states that the implementation of the Adaptive Learning Architecture will significantly improve detection accuracy compared to standard models. Constructs will be operationalized through metrics such as detection accuracy (percentage of correctly identified anomalies) and robustness against attacks (model performance metrics), evaluated against controls like standard machine learning models. The methodology will employ statistical analyses to compare performance across groups, controlling for confounding factors like data quality and model architecture. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in resilience theory, technical development of robust learning frameworks, empirical validation of adaptive mechanisms, and practical deployment guidelines addressing scalability challenges. Key limitations include potential scalability issues, real-world applicability challenges, and variability in data quality, necessitating careful consideration of confounding factors and a risk analysis to mitigate identified failure modes.
